about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: the exhibition explores the multifaceted concept of capture or subjugation through interactions with space, material, and boundaries, demonstrating different approaches to occupying and transforming the surrounding environment, whether physical or mental. territorial capture is defined from two sides in the works.
about.paragraph_2: on one side lies the territory of material, where works may display a more aggressive, direct intervention, setting clear boundaries, dominating it, and producing a local capture. on the other, they offer a softer, enveloping appropriation of space, as though lying within it, creating new forms of interaction through material and demonstrating a global intervention into the external. this intersection creates a profound contrast between two artistic approaches, drawing attention to unstable boundaries between reality and dream, hard and soft, the imaginary world and the real.
about.paragraph_3: the intuitive process of sewing becomes a method of subordinating space to artistic will and creates a sense of fluidity and uncertainty. we construct barriers in space, create new spatial connections and integrations, and emphasise different relationships with boundaries—both real and metaphorical.
about.paragraph_4: material is perceived as dynamic, evolving structures that create a living environment around themselves and symbolise a continuous process of growth and expansion, a striving for self-sufficiency. the creation of autonomous, self-reproducing artistic systems prompts reflection on different aspects of interaction with the world, on the nature of space, materiality, and boundaries, both physical and metaphorical. our individual artistic practices emerge as contrasting yet complementary approaches to occupying space.
